name: Tapo P110M (EU)

radios.note: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (IEEE 802.11b/g/n). The EU datasheet says Bluetooth is used for setup only.

matter.note: TP-Link's EU product page calls it Matter-certified. The CSA listing we found (family SKU P110M) names the UK, not the EU, variant; we found no CSA entry naming P110M(EU).

apple_home.note: TP-Link lists Apple Home. There is no HomeKit (HAP) mode, so this goes through Matter; the EU datasheet says a controller such as an Apple TV or HomePod is needed.

google_home.note: Added in the Google Home app by scanning the Matter code. Needs a Google Matter controller.

alexa.note: Added in the Alexa app through Matter. Needs an Echo that works as a Matter controller. We did not confirm whether the Tapo Alexa skill also covers this model.

smartthings.note: TP-Link lists Samsung SmartThings; setup is through Matter.

home_assistant.note: Home Assistant's TP-Link Smart Home integration lists the P110M among supported Tapo devices. It can also be added through the Matter integration.

hubRequired.note: The EU datasheet says no hub is needed with the Tapo app; third-party apps need a Matter controller.

localControl.note: TP-Link's EU page says Tapo Matter devices talk to other certified devices on the local network (LAN).

energyMonitoring.note: Real-time and historical use plus bill estimates in the Tapo app. Energy data over Matter depends on firmware and controller; TP-Link's UK store once said it was not supported over Matter yet.

maxLoadWatts.note: 16 A / 3680 W for general use and resistive loads; 1/6 HP motor. TP-Link says it is not meant for high-power motors such as air conditioners.

summary: The EU Tapo P110M is a 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi plug with energy monitoring that reaches Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings through Matter. Home Assistant can use its TP-Link integration or Matter. It is rated 16 A / 3680 W, and Bluetooth is used only for setup. The Tapo app needs no hub; third-party platforms need their own Matter controller.
caveats: Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings work through Matter, so each needs its own Matter controller.
Energy readings over Matter depend on firmware and controller; the Tapo app is the reliable place to see them.
Rated 1/6 HP for motors; TP-Link says not to use it with high-power motor appliances such as air conditioners.
